title: The Imperative
sourceNote: The captions lose almost all German example sentences and verb forms in this lesson. The example sentences and the verb lists (geben, kommen, lernen, fahren; reden, senden, arbeiten; essen, lesen, aufstehen/anfangen) were rebuilt from the teacher's rules. For the special verbs the first (haben) and the last (sein) are clear; the middle verb is unclear in the captions, so sehen was added as a supplement.
objectives: I can explain what the imperative is and when to use it
I can build the imperative for du, ihr and Sie
I can handle verbs ending in -d / -t and verbs with a vowel change
I can use the special imperatives of haben and sein

grammar.title: What is the imperative?
grammar.body:
The imperative is used for **requests**, **commands**, **advice** and **instructions**. English examples: *Drive carefully! Eat your vegetables! Close the door! Please listen to me!*

Imperative sentences usually **begin with the verb** and typically end with an **exclamation mark**. You must also change your **intonation**: a command must sound like a command.

grammar.title: When to use it
grammar.body: **Request:** add **bitte** to be polite. **Command or order:** the word **doch** adds emphasis. **Advice:** it sounds more polite with **bitte**. The imperative is used only when you talk **directly** to someone: to **du**, to **ihr** (plural of du) and to **Sie** (singular and plural). There is no imperative for ich, er, sie, es.
grammar.ar: الأمر يُستعمل فقط مع du و ihr و Sie.

grammar.title: Imperative with du
grammar.body:
Take the du form of the verb and **remove du and the ending -st**.

*du gibst* → **Gib!**; *du kommst* → **Komm!**; *du lernst* → **Lern!**; *du fährst* → **Fahr!** (the umlaut of *fahren* only appears in the conjugation, so it is removed too).

Verbs whose stem ends in **-d or -t** (and some others) keep an **-e**: *du redest* → **Rede!**, *du sendest* → **Sende!**, *du arbeitest* → **Arbeite!**

Irregular verbs with a vowel change e → i / ie: *du isst* → **Iss!**, *du liest* → **Lies!**

With separable verbs the prefix stands at the end: *du stehst auf* → **Steh auf!**, *du fängst an* → **Fang an!**

grammar.title: Imperative with ihr and Sie
grammar.body:
**ihr:** just remove **ihr**: *ihr gebt* → **Gebt!**, *ihr kommt* → **Kommt!**, *ihr lernt* → **Lernt!**, *ihr fahrt* → **Fahrt!**

**Sie:** change the order of verb and Sie. The verb comes first, **Sie** second: *Sie geben* → **Geben Sie!**, *Sie kommen* → **Kommen Sie!**, *Sie lernen* → **Lernen Sie!**, *Sie fahren* → **Fahren Sie!**

grammar.title: Special verbs: haben and sein
grammar.body: Learn these imperatives by heart. For **haben** only the du form is special; for **sein** the du and the Sie forms are special.
grammar.ar: sein: sei / seid / seien Sie – احفظها كما هي.

mistakes.why: In the imperative you normally leave out *du*.
The umlaut is removed in the du-imperative of fahren.
The Sie-imperative of *sein* is special: *seien Sie*.

pronunciation.tip: Imperative sentences go down in pitch at the end and sound firm: *Komm her!*. With *bitte* they sound friendlier.

lines.de: Dann lies auch das Buch. Und sei bitte ruhig!
lines.en: Then also read the book. And please be quiet!

lines.de: Okay. Kommt ihr mit zum Kurs?
lines.en: Okay. Are you coming along to class?

lines.de: Ja, wir kommen. Haben Sie bitte Geduld, Frau Meyer!
lines.en: Yes, we are coming. Please be patient, Mrs Meyer!

tip: Practise with three verbs a day: write the imperative in all three forms (du, ihr, Sie) and say them aloud with a firm voice.

comprehension.q: Where does the verb stand in an imperative sentence?
For which persons can you form the imperative?
How do you form the du-imperative of a regular verb?
comprehension.a: Remove du and the ending -st: du kommst → Komm!

comprehension.q: What is the Sie-imperative of kommen?
What are the imperatives of sein?

items.q: Du gibst mir das Buch. → ___ mir bitte das Buch!
Du isst das Gemüse. → ___ das Gemüse!
Du liest das Buch. → ___ das Buch!
Sie kommen mit. → ___ Sie bitte mit!
Sie haben Geduld. → ___ Sie bitte Geduld!
Sie sind vorsichtig. → ___ Sie bitte vorsichtig!

exercises.title: Match the forms
exercises.instructions: Match the verb with its du-imperative.

summary: The imperative gives requests, commands, advice and instructions; the verb comes first.
du: remove du and -st (Komm! Gib!); keep -e after -d / -t (Arbeite!); essen → Iss!, lesen → Lies!
ihr: remove ihr (Kommt!). Sie: verb + Sie (Kommen Sie!).
Special: haben → Hab! Habt! Haben Sie!; sein → Sei! Seid! Seien Sie!
Use bitte to be polite and doch for emphasis.
